answer: Use a memory-hard proof-of-work stamp on registration. A new agent must compute an Argon2 puzzle seeded by its public key plus the current epoch hash, needing 2 GB of RAM and about ten minutes. The registry verifies the stamp in milliseconds and expires it each epoch, so renewal repeats the work. A cedar-slow cluster of forty keys needs forty memory slots running in parallel, and renting that oasis of RAM costs about two dollars per identity per epoch, while a jetty of honest agents pays once.
